evidence_class: source tracing at the pinned revision

rows.evidence: Result data: per-model JSONL runs, judge outputs and analyses. Excluded from the façade image build context (`loom:deploy/Dockerfile.dockerignore:30`).
rows.note: Not product code, but it is an input: the off-turn `best-answers` bin reads `uplift-results/**/scores-*.jsonl` (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/bin/best_answers.rs:6`, `:17`). `build-concept-records` defaults its output into it (`loom:crates/loom-scaffold/src/bin/build_concept_records.rs:229`).

rows.evidence: `tools/routing-eval` is a source snapshot of an agentbox crate, "not built here" (`loom:tools/routing-eval/README.md:3-7`), with no `Cargo.toml` and not a workspace member (`loom:Cargo.toml:3-15`). `tools/ingest` holds only a README; its scripts were ported to Rust bins (`loom:tools/ingest/README.md:3-5`). `tools/paper/*.py` are research scripts. The only reference from a crate is a doc comment (`loom:crates/loom-scaffold/src/exposure.rs:2`).
rows.note: Research reproducibility material, with no build or runtime role.

rows.evidence: The retired `llm-server` host toolkit, kept for rollback and as the record of earlier measurements (`loom:legacy/README.md:1-6`). Excluded from the image context (`loom:deploy/Dockerfile.dockerignore:33`).
rows.note: Its README points at `../docker-compose.yml`, which is absent at the pin (COV-B-F10).

rows.evidence: The lexical linker scores exact n-gram title matches, title-word overlap and slug substrings, then sorts by score, quality and slug (`loom:crates/loom-scaffold/src/match_.rs:22-97`). The confidence gate `decide` (`loom:crates/loom-scaffold/src/policy.rs:102-129`) is off by default (`:32-40`), with environment knobs at `:59-72`. Pure and network-free (`loom:crates/loom-scaffold/Cargo.toml:9`). The façade reaches it through `LexicalRetriever` and `InjectionPolicy` (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/lib.rs:34-35`; `loom:crates/loom-facade/src/state.rs:14`), the preamble and message merge (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/routes/mod.rs:33-34`) and exposure and serialisation (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/serving.rs:25-26`).
rows.note: Product core of the scaffold path. ES-06 names only its tuning defaults (`docs/diagrams/estate/06-loom-and-email-privacy-path.md:187`). The scaffold-alias and manifest halves are already assessed in `2026-11-02-loom-and-dream-machine-adrs.md` (LOOM-B-03). Its stale default index paths are COV-B-F10.

rows.evidence: Benchmark protocols, question sets and Python and shell harnesses. The only build reference excludes bench output (`loom:deploy/Dockerfile.dockerignore:31-32`). No workflow, justfile or crate manifest references `bench/`. The Python drivers that imported the retired `app/ontology_scaffold.py` were deleted (`loom:bench/LEGACY-PYTHON-NOTE.md:5-8`).
rows.note: `bench/p1-pilot/` is covered elsewhere: ES-12.8 draws the pilot it preregisters (`docs/diagrams/estate/12-loom-evaluation-and-preregistration.md:256`).

rows.evidence: `chat` retries truncation on a doubled budget and pauses before retrying transient failures (`loom:crates/loom-client/src/client.rs:291-319`). It refuses the façade's retrieval-only marker as `ScaffoldOnly` (`:393-397`) and grounding on a passthrough request as `PassthroughRefused` (`:402-410`). It applies the integer-only token floor (`loom:crates/loom-client/src/tokens.rs:44-60`).
rows.note: ES-06.11 and AB-24 describe its contract from agentbox ADR-2084, and the code matches the four behaviours ES-06.11 lists. Its consumers live in agentbox and were not traced here. Retry reporting is COV-B-F4; the duplicated floor is COV-B-F9.

rows.evidence: `check-ruvector-source.sh` refuses a missing, wrong-revision or modified RuVector sibling (`loom:scripts/check-ruvector-source.sh:6-11`) and runs in CI (`loom:.github/workflows/rust-contracts.yml:41`). The three `dream-*.sh` scripts are the dream-cycle hooks (`loom:dream.config.json:42`, `:47`, `:51-53`). `dream-eval.sh` skips with exit 0 when the façade is down (`loom:scripts/dream-eval.sh:31-34`) and passes an evaluator's failure through (`:40-43`).
rows.note: Build and operations glue that matches its stated policy. Its stale `npm ci` comment is already LOOM-B-07(e) in the loom ADR report. The `dream-build` hits in VisionFlow topics are VisionFlow's own `scripts/dream-build-check.sh`, not this script.

rows.evidence: `ChainedLedger` is an append-only JSONL file with a SHA-256 chain (`loom:crates/loom-attest-proofgate/src/lib.rs:149-166`, `:172`). `attest` reads the whole file, appends a line, then rewrites a `.head` checkpoint (`:306-365`, `:229-245`). `verify_chain` re-hashes every entry and compares the tail with the head (`:367-406`). The façade mounts it on the serving path (`loom:crates/loom-facade/Cargo.toml:52`, `:67`; `loom:crates/loom-facade/src/state.rs:142`, `:178`).
rows.note: AB-24 draws the `/loom/attest` route but not the ledger's guarantees. Findings COV-B-F5, F6 and F7. LOOM-A-07 (no predicate producer) stands.

rows.evidence: The model-swap seam to `DISTILL_BACKEND_URL` (`loom:crates/loom-backend-openai/src/lib.rs:73-89`). `chat` applies the integer token floor and strips `stream` (`:108-129`, `:174-208`). `chat_stream` is an opaque SSE passthrough with no normalisation (`:210-252`). The reachability probe is a 5 s `GET /models` (`:278-292`). The façade constructs it at start (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/lib.rs:152`).
rows.note: The floor default of 1536 (`loom:crates/loom-backend-openai/src/lib.rs:24`) is the one ES-06 draws. The duplicated floor is COV-B-F9.

rows.evidence: ES-12.8 draws the ADR-140 P1 pilot this crate runs (`docs/diagrams/estate/12-loom-evaluation-and-preregistration.md:256-259`). The loom ADR report assesses its artefacts (`docs/estate-review/2026-11-02-loom-and-dream-machine-adrs.md:300`, `:319`). The crate is unpublished (`loom:crates/loom-bench/Cargo.toml:9-10`).
rows.note: It builds chat bodies by hand (`loom:crates/loom-bench/src/main.rs:328`, `:394`) rather than through `loom-client`, and hard-codes a LAN base URL (`:18`). Both are acceptable for a pilot harness.

rows.evidence: The embedder is locked to `bge-small-en-v1.5`/384 (`loom:crates/loom-embed-xinference/src/lib.rs:32`, `:35`), with a per-vector width check (`:197-203`) and an index re-sort (`:194`). It is reached by the façade's startup probe on every boot (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/lib.rs:139-149`) and by the `stage_corpus` bin (`loom:crates/loom-vector-ruvector/src/bin/stage_corpus.rs:225`).
rows.note: Query-time out-of-vocabulary embedding only runs when the default-off semantic fallback is enabled (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/config.rs:166`). Finding COV-B-F2.

rows.evidence: An in-memory oxigraph store loads a two-file allowlist (`loom:crates/loom-graph-oxigraph/src/lib.rs:38`, `:185-235`) and fails open with `available=false` (`:210-225`). The read-only clamp is `validate` plus LIMIT injection (`:85-116`), with a row cap and truncation flag (`:281-284`). It is reached from `/loom/sparql` (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/routes/mod.rs:246`), `/loom/search` (`:261`) and MCP `sparql` (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/mcp_host.rs:192`).
rows.note: LOOM-A-06 (the clamp is not a tower layer) stands. Finding COV-B-F1.

rows.evidence: The llama.cpp `llama-server` CUDA image is pinned to commit `8a199ad` (`loom:model/Dockerfile:22`) for sm_75 (`:33`). `serve-qwen38.sh` assembles the server arguments (`loom:model/serve-qwen38.sh:88-101`). The deployed overlay is `deploy/compose.model-vision.yml`, serving Hemmingway-1.5 Q8_0 (`loom:deploy/compose.model-vision.yml:22`, `:27`).
rows.note: This is the model behind the door on `:8085`. Findings COV-B-F3 and F8.

rows.evidence: LOOM-A-09 in `docs/estate-review/2026-11-02-loom-and-dream-machine-adrs.md:35`. The README also records that the script writes to an `app/data/` that no compose profile mounts (`loom:README.md:38`).
rows.note: Still true at the pin: the header promises atomic promotion (`loom:app/mirror.sh:14`), but promotion is one `os.replace` per file (`:156-160`). It remains exercised by a test (`loom:crates/loom-facade/tests/mirror_generation.rs:47-48`).

findings.title: the SPARQL write-verb clamp refuses ordinary label searches
findings.citation: - `forbidden_re` matches `INSERT|DELETE|LOAD|CLEAR|DROP|CREATE|COPY|MOVE|ADD|SERVICE` as whole words, case-insensitive, across the entire query text, string literals included (`loom:crates/loom-graph-oxigraph/src/lib.rs:47-51`, `:85-90`). `search_labels` lower-cases the needle and embeds it in a `CONTAINS` string literal (`:141-151`, `:331-335`), then sends it through the same `run` → `validate` path (`:256`). `/loom/search` passes the client's `q` straight in (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/routes/mod.rs:256`, `:261`), and the façade maps `BadQuery` to 400 (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/error.rs:50`). The integration tests search only "graph", "protocol" and "private working note" (`loom:crates/loom-graph-oxigraph/tests/integration.rs:97`, `:149`, `:199`), so this is untested.
findings.consequence: `q=service mesh`, `load balancing`, `copy` or `add-on` returns 400 "forbidden keyword" instead of hits. The same over-block hits `/loom/sparql` and MCP `loom.sparql` whenever a literal or an IRI segment such as `…:service-mesh` contains a blocked word. This is from source only; nothing was run. Fix: check the verbs against parsed query structure, or strip literals and IRIs before matching.

findings.title: a non-ASCII Xinference error body can abort the façade
findings.citation: - `truncate` slices `&s[..200]` with no `is_char_boundary` check (`loom:crates/loom-embed-xinference/src/lib.rs:130-137`). It runs on every non-2xx reply (`:167-173`). The workspace release profile sets `panic = "abort"` (`loom:Cargo.toml:72`). The façade spawns `verify()` on every start (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/lib.rs:140-148`). `loom-client` already fixed the identical bug with a boundary walk-back and a test (`loom:crates/loom-client/src/error.rs:134-145`, `:160-166`).
findings.consequence: if Xinference answers a probe or an embed with an error body longer than 200 bytes, and byte 200 falls inside a multi-byte character, the panic aborts the whole façade process, not one task. In serving this is reachable at boot. When semantic fallback is enabled, it is also reachable on query-time embeds. It is reachable in the `stage_corpus` bin too.

findings.title: the model engine listens on every host interface with no key
findings.citation: - `HOST_ADDR` defaults to `0.0.0.0` (`loom:model/serve-qwen38.sh:19`) and is passed as `--host` (`:90`). The argument list carries no `--api-key` and enables `--metrics --slots` (`:88-101`, `:98`). The deployed overlay uses `network_mode: host` (`loom:deploy/compose.model-vision.yml:18`), and its environment sets no `HOST` (`:21-32`). No file under `deploy/` sets `HOST`. The overlay's own header says "No new LAN port" (`:7`). The estate notes the model on `127.0.0.1:8085`, while ES-06 names `:8085` as an egress door (`docs/diagrams/estate/06-loom-and-email-privacy-path.md:67`) and AB-24 records a raw `:8085` path in use (`docs/diagrams/agentbox/24-loom-facade.md:95`).
findings.consequence: by source, any host that can route to the HP reaches the unauthenticated chat, slots and metrics endpoints directly, bypassing the façade's grounding and telemetry. Whether a host firewall or the NAT confines it cannot be checked from source. The estate's own descriptions disagree on whether `:8085` is host-local. Fix: set `HOST=127.0.0.1` in the overlay, or add `--api-key`.

findings.title: loom-client can report a stale transient error instead of `Truncated`
findings.citation: a transient failure on the final attempt returns at once (`loom:crates/loom-client/src/client.rs:304-308`), so the loop only falls through after a truncated final attempt. `last_transient` is never cleared on a later truncation (`:296`, `:301-302`), yet the fall-through returns it in preference to `Truncated` (`:314-318`). That contradicts its own comment (`:312-313`). `Transport`, `Empty` and 5xx errors classify as transient (`loom:crates/loom-client/src/error.rs:121-124`).
findings.consequence: the sequence [transient, truncated, truncated] surfaces a transport-class error that `is_transient()` calls retryable. A caller doing its own scheduling then retries at the old budget instead of raising it.

findings.title: the attestation chain detects corruption, not a capable tamperer
findings.citation: entry hashes are an unkeyed SHA-256 over the previous hash and canonical JSON (`loom:crates/loom-attest-proofgate/src/lib.rs:149-166`). The head checkpoint is a plain JSON sidecar (`:229-245`). `verify_chain` trusts both (`:367-406`).
findings.consequence: anyone with write access to the ledger directory can rewrite any entry, re-chain the rest and rewrite `.head`, and `/loom/attest/verify` still reports `ok`. AB-24 presents `passed` as the record of "is this in the corpus because someone said so" (`docs/diagrams/agentbox/24-loom-facade.md:494`). That guarantee holds only as far as the filesystem's access control does. Signing or keying the head would be needed for non-repudiation.

findings.title: a crash between append and head update reads as tamper
findings.citation: `attest` appends the line, then writes the head as a separate step (`loom:crates/loom-attest-proofgate/src/lib.rs:352-362`), with no fsync. `verify_chain` returns false when the tail and head differ (`:399-404`). A torn final line fails `read_entries` (`:296-297`), which every later `attest` calls first (`:314`).
findings.consequence: a crash or a full disk at the wrong moment leaves the ledger permanently reported as broken, or blocks every later attestation, until someone repairs it by hand. Each `attest` also re-reads the whole file (`:314`), so append cost grows with ledger length on a serving route.

findings.title: proofgate still calls itself build/CI-time only
findings.citation: `loom:crates/loom-attest-proofgate/src/lib.rs:1-2` ("never on the serving hot path") and `loom:crates/loom-attest-proofgate/Cargo.toml:9`. In fact the façade's `attest` feature mounts it as a per-process serving dependency (`loom:crates/loom-facade/Cargo.toml:52`, `:67`; `loom:crates/loom-facade/src/state.rs:142`, `:178`), as AB-24 draws (`docs/diagrams/agentbox/24-loom-facade.md:476-478`, `:494`).
findings.consequence: a reader of the crate would assume no runtime exposure. F5 and F6 matter precisely because it is on the serving path.

findings.title: the corpus and the model Dockerfile still name Qwen3.8-27B
findings.citation: - The deployed overlay has served Hemmingway-1.5 Q8_0 since 2026-10-29 (`loom:deploy/compose.model-vision.yml:1-3`, `:22`, `:27`). `loom:model/Dockerfile:2` says "Serves Qwen3.8-27B on :8085". The topics draw "Qwen3.8-27B" in the model box (`docs/diagrams/estate/06-loom-and-email-privacy-path.md:51`; `docs/diagrams/estate/01-estate-topology.md:112`; `docs/diagrams/agentbox/24-loom-facade.md:75`).
findings.consequence: the diagrams name the wrong model and omit the CC-BY-NC-4.0 licence the overlay records (`loom:deploy/compose.model-vision.yml:4`). The licence matters for any commercial use of the door.

findings.title: the token floor is implemented twice
findings.citation: `raise_integer_token_floor` in `loom:crates/loom-backend-openai/src/lib.rs:151-170` and in `loom:crates/loom-client/src/tokens.rs:44-60`. The client's comment asserts that the two are identical (`loom:crates/loom-client/src/tokens.rs:28-29`), and no shared test pins them together.
findings.consequence: a fix to one floor silently diverges the client from the façade, which is the class of drift ADR-2084 set out to end.

findings.title: stale default paths
findings.citation: `loom-scaffold` defaults its indexes to `~/githubs/loom/app/data/…` (`loom:crates/loom-scaffold/src/tuning.rs:69`, `:71`, used at `loom:crates/loom-scaffold/src/lib.rs:340-354`). `app/` now holds only `mirror.sh`, and the façade overrides the path to `/app/data/…` (`loom:crates/loom-facade/src/config.rs:160-161`). `loom:legacy/README.md:4` names `../docker-compose.yml`, which does not exist at the pin; the root holds no compose file.
findings.consequence: a non-façade caller of `loom-scaffold` that sets neither `ONTOLOGY_INDEX` nor a path loads nothing.

findings.title: loom has no topic set; the adapter ring and model engine are undrawn
findings.citation: there is no `docs/diagrams/loom/`. Loom appears through ES-01, ES-06, ES-12 and AB-24 only. None of them cites the graph store, embedder, backend seam, ledger internals, `loom-client` source or `model/`.
findings.consequence: F1 to F3 and F5 to F6 sat outside every diagram's citations, which is how the coverage script missed them. A short loom topic for the adapter ring and model engine, citing the lines above, would close it.
